correctness.rationale: Every positive periodic orbit has multipliers U_i=q nu_p(n_i)+p nu_q(n_i)>0 satisfying product U_i=(pq)^L; this forces each U_i to have support only among {p,q}. Prime-valuation updates derive the exact T(U) transition. A three-case proof shows that for every p,q-smooth U>pq, T(U)>pq; cyclicity then contradicts product equality unless U_i=pq for all i. The resulting fixed-point equation has only exponent pairs (p,0) and (0,q). All hypotheses, positivity and k>=1 are explicit. Finite verifier separately checks representative thresholds and fixed points; it is not used to infer the infinite statement.

value.rationale: This resolves the first genuinely multi-prime support size in the natural study of periodic points of arithmetic subderivatives. The all-prime-pair theorem is an infinite structural classification, strictly stronger than the known {2,3} case and independent of the already known fixed-point equation. The exact smooth-multiplier invariant is a reusable mechanism; the result directly addresses a published periodic-point research direction. It makes no unsupported statement for three or more supported primes.
